findings.quote: No slip reaches 49%: subtracting the first four seconds' distance from the height gives 64%, and using the final speed alone as a fraction of the height gives 40%; nothing lands on 49%.
findings.note: Subtracting the first four seconds' distance from the height is the correct method: 125 − 80 = 45 m, which is 36%, the right answer. The entry attaches 64% to it (that is 80/125, the first four seconds' distance itself) and lists it among the mistakes, so a student who used the correct route is told it fails.
findings.fix: No slip reaches 49%: taking the first four seconds' distance itself as the fraction gives 64%, and using the final speed alone as a fraction of the height gives 40%; nothing lands on 49%.

notes: t = 5 s, last-second distance = 5(25 − 16) = 45 m, x = 45/125 × 100 = 36. The 40% figure in the same entry is right, since the final speed is 50 m s⁻¹ and 50/125 = 40%. The entry for option 1 lands on 9 exactly (5² − 4² read as the percentage) and the entry for option 3 lands on 25 exactly (9/36 in place of 9/25). A pairwise search over the fall time, the height, the last-second and first-four-second distances, the nth-second numbers and the g = 9.8 variants found no route to 49, so that part of the entry is sound.
